name: MCPJam Backend guest session mints >1200/h sustained
description: WARN · More than 1,200 guest sessions minted per hour, sustained over two checks (~30 min). Not a page.

Volume alone cannot tell abuse from a good day here: legit peaks (1,125/h) nearly touch the observed abuse rate (1,036-1,138/h). Confirm against the spend and bucket-drain monitors before acting on this one.
TRIAGE: Railway edge logs — srcIp + clientUa on /api/web/guest-session. One user-agent or one /16 spread across many IPs is one operator.
rationale: WHY THIS EXISTS: requested as a direct volume signal on the minting route. Caveat, measured: it is a WEAK signal. Legit hours reach 1,125 (09-08) and 3-hour peaks 2,101; the 09-15 wave peaked at 1,038/h (16,325/day spread evenly). This monitor would NOT have fired on 09-15. What catches that wave is 'distinct FREE-allowance spenders', 'free buckets drained' and 'scenario redeems' — minted guests that go on to SPEND. Treat a page here as 'something is hammering the mint route hard' (a scraper, a broken client loop, a bigger farm), not as the abuse detector.
WHY THIS THRESHOLD: 1,200/h is above every legit hour observed 08-25..09-16; the 2-of-2 debounce means a single launch spike that clears within 15 minutes does not post.

NOTE ON 'positive results': triggerAfterNPositiveResults is a DEBOUNCE (fire only after N consecutive positive checks). It makes a monitor slower, never louder; Axiom notifies once on entering the alert state and once on leaving. Page-vs-warn is decided by the notifier, not this field.
